title: Spike orthogonalization — labbook
body:
Goal:
Quick notebook for an experiment I hacked together to "orthogonalize" client arrival spikes so they have reduced overlap at the server ingress. Idea is to see whether small client-side jitter + tokenized request shaping reduces p99 tail and eviction pressure on hot KV caches without hurting aggregate throughput.

Notes to self / context:
- Running on dedicated dev cluster (4xA100 equiv), redwood-serve v0.62 branch.
- Model: redwood-v2-7b-quant (fp16->4-bit emulate path).
- Workload: synthetic spike bursts (50–800 QPS instantaneous), 128 token requests, mean payload 300 tokens, Zipf alpha=1.1 for tenant mix.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU %util, KV cache hit-rate, queue length, batch size distribution.

Experiment config (three treatments):
1) baseline: synchronized spike injector (all clients hit at same epoch), no jitter.
2) jittered: per-client uniform jitter in [0, 200ms] added to each request at client-side.
3) shaped: orthogonalized pulses: algorithm spreads N-arrivals into k micro-windows using lightweight deterministic offsets (see below).

Shaping algorithm (toy):
- For a burst of size B arriving at t0, pick k = max(2, min(8, floor(B/64))).
- Compute offsets = {0, delta, 2*delta, ...} with delta = 20ms * (8/k).
- Assign arrival times = t0 + offsets[(client_id mod k)] + small uniform ±5ms noise.

Run log (timestamps local):
2025-02-12T09:05 — Baseline run (3x repeats):
- peak ingress: 780 qps (instant), sustained 12s
- p50: 18ms, p95: 123ms, p99: 468ms
- KV cache hit-rate: 68%
- observed long tail correlated with simultaneous batch construction spikes; batch sizes peaked at 18 tokens/request per GPU slice

2025-02-12T09:40 — Jittered run (3x repeats):
- peak ingress: 780 qps (instant), sustained 12s
- p50: 20ms, p95: 96ms, p99: 312ms
- KV cache hit-rate: 66% (slight drop due to desync across tenants)
- batch size distribution smoothed; fewer extreme batch construction events

2025-02-12T10:15 — Shaped run (3x repeats):
- peak ingress: 780 qps, sustained 12s
- p50: 22ms, p95: 74ms, p99: 146ms
- KV cache hit-rate: 71% (improved; hypothesized due to reduced eviction bursts)
- queue length tail substantially smaller; batch sizes more consistent (median 6, max 10)

Quick ASCII sketch - p99 across runs (lower is better):
  Baseline  |█████████████████████████ 468ms
  Jittered  |█████████████████ 312ms
  Shaped    |███████ 146ms

Observations / hypotheses:
- Simple per-client uniform jitter gives nontrivial tail reduction (~33% p99 improvement) by breaking perfect alignment.
- Deterministic shaping (orthogonalization) dramatically reduces p99 (≈69% vs baseline) while preserving or slightly improving KV hit-rate. Hypothesis: spreading arrivals reduces instantaneous working set pressure on KV eviction, which prevents repeated cache churn and large batch spikes.
- Shaping increased p50/p95 slightly in some runs (couple ms) — tradeoff: smoother but slightly higher median latency due to intentional spreading. Worth it if SLO focuses on tail.
- GPU utilization stayed within 70–82% across treatments; shaping reduced spikes in utilization (smoother curve).

Instrumentation notes:
- Collected pprof traces for worst baseline run — saw large locks at batch construction and mutex contention on request queue.
- Flame graph shows batcher goroutine contending when many arrivals coalesce into one batch.
- Added lightweight tagging to requests with "shape_id" to validate offsets; logs show correct distribution.

Next steps / TODO:
- Run same experiment with cold KV cache start (restart cache between repeats) — see if effect amplified.
- Test with mixed-size requests (short prompts interleaved with long) to measure fairness effects.
- Try randomized k selection and adaptive shaping probing (autoscale k based on instantaneous ingress).
- Open a short spike into infra team for a micro-batching counter-proposal: dynamic batch window shrink when hatch detected. Link: https://linear.app/ENGINF/ISSUE-3241
- If results reproduce, add shaping as a client-side library option for SDK (opt-in) and as an egress feature for dedicated customers via 'ingress-tempering' setting.

Questions / unresolved:
- Why did KV hit-rate improve with shaping vs baseline? Need to instrument eviction counters more precisely (per-shard).
- Is there an adverse effect on throughput for very large sustained bursts (>2k qps)? schedule bigger runs.

Scratch of commands used:
- run harness: ./tools/spike-harness --config=cfg/spike-780.yaml --reps=3 --tag=orthogonal-test
- collect metrics: ./tools/collect-metrics --from=2025-02-12T09:00 --to=2025-02-12T11:00 --out=run-orthogonal-metrics.json

Notes to self: keep this notebook short; convert to a proper runbook if shaping looks stable. Potential low-effort win for hosted customers where we can recommend SDK opt-ins.

End.
